sections: dream · /drim/ · noun · Word · New
images or events that you experience in your mind while sleeping. I had a dream about the sea.
quiet · /ˈkwaɪət/ · adjective · Word · New
making little or no noise. The bedroom is quiet at night.
asleep · /əˈslip/ · adjective · Word · New
sleeping, rather than awake. The baby is asleep.
pajamas · /pəˈdʒæməz/ · plural noun · Word · New
loose clothes worn for sleeping. Put on your pajamas before bed.
fall asleep · /ˌfɔl əˈslip/ · verb phrase · Phrase · New
to begin sleeping. I fall asleep at ten.

articulation.alt: sleep: /s/ → /l/ → /i/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
/l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.

cards.title: Read and write
sections: Reading

Puck puts on his pajamas and reads in a quiet room. He feels ready for bed. He falls asleep at ten. Later, Heart checks that the baby is asleep too and closes the door softly. In the morning, Puck remembers a dream about walking by the sea.
Find the answer
When does Puck begin sleeping, and what does he remember in the morning?
Write
Write two sentences using two words from today’s new word bank.
